title: Drip Irrigation

segments.say: More than eighty per cent of India's available water goes to irrigation. So how a farm waters its crops matters to everyone.

numbers.sub: of India's water used for irrigation

right.title: Drip
items: water goes to each plant's roots

segments.say: In flood irrigation, the whole field is soaked and much of the water is lost. Drip irrigation sends water only where the plant needs it.
It works through pipes laid along the rows, with small drippers that release water straight into the root zone.
Besides saving water, drip cuts the use of fertiliser, lowers labour costs, and studies report better yields and incomes.

anim.title: Per Drop More Crop
items: 55% help for small and marginal farmers

segments.say: Since twenty fifteen, the Per Drop More Crop scheme has paid part of the cost: fifty-five per cent for small and marginal farmers, forty-five for others.

anim.below: of net sown area under micro-irrigation (July 2026)

segments.say: By July twenty twenty-six, it had brought about a hundred and fifteen lakh hectares under micro-irrigation. That is still only about eight per cent of India's net sown area.
For GS Three, link drip to water-use efficiency, and remember the scheme's own slogan: more crop per drop.

sources: PIB backgrounder, August 2026, 'Water-Smart Farming with Per Drop More Crop': more than 80% of India's available water resources are used for irrigation; about 50% of net sown area irrigated; micro-irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone; drip irrigates the root zone through emitters on lateral tubes; 55% assistance for small and marginal farmers and 45% for others; PDMC named so from 2015-16 to 2021-22 under PMKSY; 115 lakh hectares under micro-irrigation as of July 2026, about 8.11% of net sown area; independent studies report higher yields, water savings, lower costs and higher incomes
PIB, 2020 (PRID 1630606): PMKSY-PDMC focuses on water-use efficiency through drip and sprinkler systems; drip saves water and reduces fertiliser use, labour and other input costs

reviewNote: Facts are from two PIB documents; the 2026 backgrounder is the main source. Flooding 'loses much water' is a plain-words summary of the PIB point that micro-irrigation reduces wastage. Moving facts: area under micro-irrigation, and the scheme's current home (PIB says it is now within a wider scheme).
